_: The Holm's rock tip in 1989 (docs/town-plan.md, the centre in detail, 6: 'At the tip, on bare rock, the old customs house and harbour master's office in small red wooden buildings, and a landing for the Penny Ferry'; centre_land.py OUTCROPS, the Holm's rock tip). Nature's first element, rock and land, is judged here. Every value is a FIXTURE VALUE until the engine provides it (docs/engine-requests.md). Local site metres: x east, y north, z up over mean sea level; the origin is the outcrop's centre, street (-246, -246) (street x = -246 - y, street y = -246 + x). Compass bearings in degrees (0 north, clockwise), dips from the horizontal.

sea._: Stavanger's spring range about 0.46 m (docs/research/land-rock-and-water.md, 3); the tip faces the Roads (fetch about 3 km to the north) on its north and west, the Basin's mouth behind the breakwater on its east.

rock.kind_why: the pack's slate is the town's own phyllite (packs/stavanger-1989/materials/slate.json; docs/stone.md)

ice._: The ice's way over the tip: toward the south-south-west (NGU Bulletin 411: southward striae on Jaeren through most of the Weichselian; secondary). Stoss (abraded, smooth) faces the north-north-east, the sea; the lee (plucked, stepped) faces the Holm.

sheeting._: unloading joints near the ground's own slope, thin near the top and thicker with depth (the corner's fixture)

outcrop._: The tip as the plan has it (centre_land.py OUTCROPS: radius 26 north-south and 36 east-west, top 7, falling at its edge over about 10 m; after Tinganes, Torshavn): one broad back of bare rock the ice wore, its lee running on into the Holm Street's end, a skerry off its north-east corner. The steep joint families that bound its blocks at this scale are the open master joints (spacings inferred; the finer joints are seams on the faces). FIXTURE VALUES.

knobs._: a skerry off the north-east corner, parted by a sound

outcrop._families: The open master joints that bound the blocks at this scale: the foliation and the two cross joints at wide angles to it (J2 runs within 25 degrees of the foliation's strike and is left to the faces as seams). 'open': the share of joints the frost and the sea opened, and their width range in metres; the rest are tight seams of tightM.

coast._: blocks under belowM at the waterline taken by the sea, share times the side's exposure

chamfers._: [min width, max width, lean] of the worn top edge by joint kind: a tight seam's narrow bevel, an open joint's round-over into its gully (on the stoss, where the ice wore it flush, stossShare of that); never more than capShare of the block's least width; a blasted face keeps its edge

sheets._: sheeting shells stripped from the stoss: thickness, the most stripped over a block, the slow field's cell (m)

opening._: How far the frost and the sea opened an open joint, by the height of the ground over it as a share of its back's top: fully below fullBelow, shut to a tight seam above shutAbove, smoothly between (the ice planed the crest across its joints; the sea and the frost open them toward the shore). A joint runs only along its trace (traceM, [min, max] of its length, about a seeded middle): past its ends the rock is whole, so the families meet in T's, not a grid.

backs._: Each block the showing joints bound was worn by the ice as a whaleback of its own (outcrop.py Back): its crest crestShift of its half-length toward its down-ice end, its back falling under the envelope to its plan's edge by a share of its half-width (rollShare, within rollM metres) with the profile's power, falling only leeShare of that down-ice of its crest, so it keeps a firm lip over its plucked lee (a plucked tread itself rounded only leeRoll of that), so a few big backs, more middle and many small ones each read as one rounded form.

acts.what: the customs house's plinth of dry stone laid on the rock, taking up its slope (rebuilt after the Holm's fire of 1860)
the Penny Ferry's landing: a short quay of split stone on the tip's east side, filled behind to an apron
the path from the landing up to the customs house, blasted into the rock's east flank, hand-drilled
the harbour master's office's plinth on the rock's west shoulder

buildings.what: the old customs house, one and a half storeys, red-painted timber, white trim
the harbour master's office, one storey, red-painted timber

breakwater._: from the Holm's north-east corner over the Basin's mouth, a light at its end (centre_land.py BREAKWATER, LIGHT)

far._: what stands beyond, from centre_land.py, for the frame's back: the beacon islet, a skerry, the small island, Bridge Island; and Herring Hill's point with the Bluff, its 20 m face over the Roads, as centre_land.py's heights draw it (site region [x0, y0, x1, y1], on a grid of stepM)

holm._: the Holm behind the tip, as a stand-in for the frame: Holm Street's end on the spine, the pub quays either side (town-plan.md, 6: two levels about six metres apart)
